# Spaces fixtures

Inputs for the verified Spaces browsing tests (`src/main/spaces-resolver.test.js`
and `src/main/spaces/*.test.js`). They live outside `src/` so packaged builds
never contain them.

## Real relay answers, 2026-10-15

`relay-anchors-2026-10-15.json` holds what the four upstream certrelay relays
(cosmos, atlas, orion and pulsar, version 0.2.11) answered on `GET /anchors` at
21:35:23Z: each relay's signed `x-anchor-root`, `x-anchor-height` and
`x-anchor-sig` headers and the 60-anchor body, which was byte-identical from
all four. All four signed root `50e07f…` at height 971604. `newestBlockHeader`
is Blockstream's `/api/block/<hash>/header` answer for that newest anchor's
block, mined at 17:24:03Z. `previousSet` is the set cosmos and atlas signed
earlier the same day (root `a9fc2a…` at 971568), with its own newest header,
so the tests can make real, validly signed relays disagree.

`query-yahoo-cosmos.bin` and `query-yahoo-atlas.bin` are the bodies of
`GET /query?q=%40yahoo` from cosmos and atlas at 21:35:41Z; they verify against
the 971604 set at anchors 970596 and 970560. `query-absent-cosmos.bin` is
cosmos's answer for `@freedomabsentprobe7`, a name nobody holds, at 21:40:45Z.

## Generated chains

At the original fixture capture, no live space published signed records. These
cryptographic unit tests use a simulated chain. `generated-chain.json` is the output of
`freedom_spaces_fixture.rs`, an example program for libveritas's own test
utilities: one root space `@example` with no delegate, owner-signed record sets
(a website, a website with a path, a second website at sequence 2, and refused
variants), one set signed by an unrelated key and one signed for another name,
plus `@delegated`, whose delegate signs a website. The messages verify
without dev mode. Every `libveritas_testutil` key comes from one zero-seeded
generator, so the output is deterministic.

Regenerate from a checkout of https://github.com/spacesprotocol/libveritas at
source commit `d2cb558830adfdfcc44613591d2c0329160fcd3b` (Rust 1.90 or later;
the 2026-10-15 run used `rust:1.91-bookworm`):

```sh
cp freedom_spaces_fixture.rs <libveritas>/testutil/examples/
cd <libveritas>
cargo run --locked -p libveritas_testutil --example freedom_spaces_fixture > generated-chain.json
```

## Member proofs

`freedom_spaces_member_fixture.rs` generates deterministic member proofs at a
first commitment, both before and after finality, and a temporary member. It
uses the published 0.4.5 package's exact source commit
`d2cb558830adfdfcc44613591d2c0329160fcd3b`, rather than relying on a mutable tag.
Every variant is checked using production verifier options. First commitments
need no ZK receipt, so no fake receipt or dev mode is used. Owner-record variants
cover valid HTTPS websites, newer sequences, invalid websites and signatures
under another key or name. The parent also has a signed website to test that it
cannot substitute for the member's records.

The hosted `Spaces member proof fixtures` workflow runs the generator using
Rust 1.91.0 and retains the JSON, build log, exact source identities and input
digests. It is fixture generation only; it does not build or replace a browser
dependency and does not establish live member acceptance.

`generated-members.json` was generated by run
[`39835555196`, attempt 1](https://github.com/pirate-social-club/freedom-browser/actions/runs/39835555196)
from Freedom `3a69c6ddf824015d5749a13fe545dbe73941c4e0`.
Its SHA-256 is `64f3a8a22bc5ee20199637976a36bf2793360f5419500110913f6d016993cf06`.
The downloaded provenance ZIP is SHA-256
`fecf284a4898231649853286737777a93a26420085a5ffc96ae5eb8dea727f3d`;
its generator digest matches the committed Rust file, and its upstream source
identity matches the pinned package source. Future hosted runs compare the
generated JSON with the checked-in fixture and fail on a mismatch.
